title: Alzheimer Genetics: APOE ε4, Presenilins and the CSF Aβ42/40 Ratio
summary: Read an APOE genotype as a risk estimate, separate it from rare familial APP/PSEN disease, see why CSF Aβ42/40 falls in Alzheimer disease, and why APOE genotyping now guides anti-amyloid therapy safety.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 73 Hits 2 and 11 and Traps 4–5 (first lesson for Ch. 73). Checked against Liu 2013, Hansson 2019 and Jeon 2025. The reviewer’s “2–5-fold / 12–15-fold” is consistent with Liu’s ORs (2.6–3.2 / 14.9); the age-specific penetrance figures (~30% by 75, >50% by 85) were not verified. Not taught: Aβ42 neurotoxicity vs Aβ40 neuroprotection and the PSEN Aβ42:Aβ40 shift (Hit 3), the ACE claim (Hit 7, Trap 2; see register rv-ace-ad), aducanumab’s discontinuation and the cholinergic drug list, psychiatric CNVs, alcohol and lithium genetics.

objectives: Name the three common APOE alleles and the residues that distinguish them.
Interpret APOE ε4 as a risk factor and contrast it with familial APP/PSEN1/PSEN2 disease.
Explain the CSF Aβ42/40 ratio and the role of APOE genotyping before anti-amyloid therapy.

scenes.title: Two APOE requests
scenes.altText: Two invented requisitions for APOE genotyping. Request 1: a healthy 58-year-old whose parent had Alzheimer disease writes “Will I get Alzheimer’s?”. Request 2: a neurologist orders APOE before starting an anti-amyloid antibody (donanemab) in a patient with early symptomatic Alzheimer disease. Question token: “What can an APOE genotype actually tell each of them?”

cues.text: Two requests for APOE genotyping arrive. A healthy 58-year-old whose parent had Alzheimer disease asks: will I get it?
And a neurologist wants APOE before starting an anti-amyloid antibody in a patient who already has early Alzheimer disease.
What can an APOE genotype actually tell each of them?

props.label: What can APOE genotype tell each?

scenes.title: Three APOE alleles and the amyloid peptide
scenes.altText: Allele card (Liu 2013): APOE has three common alleles — ε2, ε3, ε4 — worldwide frequency 8.4%, 77.9% and 13.7%. The ApoE protein (299 amino acids, ~34 kDa) differs only at residues 112 and 158: ApoE2 Cys112/Cys158; ApoE3 Cys112/Arg158; ApoE4 Arg112/Arg158. ApoE carries lipids between cells via LDL-receptor-family receptors and also binds amyloid-β (Aβ). Peptide card (Liu 2013): Aβ is 40 or 42 amino acids long, cut from amyloid precursor protein (APP) by enzymes including the γ-secretase complex, whose essential components include presenilin 1 and 2. Schematic only.

cues.text: The APOE gene has three common alleles: epsilon 2, 3 and 4. Epsilon 3 is by far the most common, at about 78 percent of alleles worldwide; epsilon 4 is about 14 percent.
The proteins differ at just two positions, 112 and 158. ApoE2 has cysteine at both, ApoE3 cysteine then arginine, and ApoE4 arginine at both.
ApoE carries lipids between cells, and it also binds amyloid beta.
Amyloid beta is a peptide of 40 or 42 amino acids, cut from amyloid precursor protein by enzymes including gamma-secretase, which is built around presenilin 1 or 2.

scenes.title: Risk allele vs causal mutation
scenes.altText: Odds card (Liu 2013, meta-analysis, Caucasian subjects, vs ε3/ε3): ε3/ε4 OR 3.2; ε2/ε4 OR 2.6; ε4/ε4 OR 14.9; ε2/ε3 OR 0.6 (protective). Ancestry token: ε4/ε4 OR 12.5 (Caucasian) vs 33.1 (Japanese), 5.7 (African American), 2.2 (Hispanic). ε4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset AD and is found in ~40% of AD patients vs 13.7% of alleles worldwide. Familial card (Liu 2013): early-onset familial AD, typically before 65, is < 1% of AD and is mainly caused by APP, PSEN1 or PSEN2 mutations that cause Aβ overproduction.

cues.text: Compared with epsilon 3 3, one epsilon 4 allele raises the odds of Alzheimer disease about three-fold, and two copies about fifteen-fold, in one large meta-analysis.
Epsilon 2 lowers the odds, an odds ratio of about 0.6. And the size of the epsilon 4 effect varies with ancestry.
So epsilon 4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer disease. Risk factor, not diagnosis.
Familial early-onset Alzheimer disease is different: mutations in APP, PSEN1 or PSEN2 drive overproduction of amyloid beta.
But these families are rare: under 1 percent of all Alzheimer disease.

props.label: ε4/ε4 OR varies: 2.2 to 33.1 by ancestry

scenes.title: What the laboratory measures
scenes.altText: CSF card (Hansson 2019): in Alzheimer dementia CSF Aβ42 is decreased while Aβ40 does not differ; the Aβ42/40 ratio normalizes Aβ42 for total Aβ (Aβ40 is the most abundant isoform) and classifies more patients correctly, including agreement with amyloid PET; collection tubes, handling and storage are critical pre-analytical factors. Liu 2013: ε4 carriers have lower CSF Aβ42. Therapy card (Jeon 2025): lecanemab was FDA-approved in July 2023 and donanemab in 2024; the donanemab Appropriate Use Recommendations require APOE genotyping for ARIA (amyloid-related imaging abnormalities) risk management. Hook answers: Request 1 — APOE gives a risk estimate, not a yes/no; Request 2 — APOE informs ARIA safety planning.

cues.text: In the laboratory, cerebrospinal fluid amyloid beta 42 falls in Alzheimer dementia, while amyloid beta 40 stays about the same.
Dividing 42 by 40 corrects for how much amyloid beta a person makes overall, and the ratio classifies more patients correctly. Tubes, handling and storage matter a lot for these assays.
APOE genotyping now has a treatment role too. Lecanemab and donanemab are approved anti-amyloid antibodies, and the donanemab recommendations require APOE genotyping to manage the risk of ARIA.
So for the healthy 58-year-old, APOE gives a risk estimate, not a yes or no. For the patient starting donanemab, it informs safety planning.

props.label: Hook: risk estimate (not yes/no) · ARIA safety planning

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “APOE ε4 means you will develop Alzheimer disease” (✓ it raises the odds — OR ~3 for one copy, ~15 for two vs ε3/ε3 — it is a risk factor, not a diagnosis); “APP/PSEN mutations explain most Alzheimer disease” (✓ familial early-onset AD is < 1% of cases); “Only four drugs are FDA-approved for AD” (✓ lecanemab (2023) and donanemab (2024) anti-amyloid antibodies were approved later).

cues.text: Trap one: APOE epsilon 4 means you will develop Alzheimer disease. No: it raises the odds, about three-fold for one copy and fifteen-fold for two. It is a risk factor, not a diagnosis.
Trap two: APP and presenilin mutations explain most Alzheimer disease. No: familial early-onset disease is under 1 percent of cases.
Trap three: only four drugs are approved. No: lecanemab in 2023 and donanemab in 2024 joined the list as anti-amyloid antibodies.

scenes.title: Two Rs = Risk
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “ApoE4 has two Rs (Arg112, Arg158) — Risk, Risk. ApoE2 has two Cs — Cushioned (protective). ApoE3 is the common middle, C then R.” Tokens: ε4 = Arg/Arg · ε3 = Cys/Arg · ε2 = Cys/Cys. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: ApoE4 has two R’s, arginine at 112 and 158: risk, risk. ApoE2 has two C’s, cysteines: cushioned. ApoE3 is the common middle, C then R.

Where it breaks: the size of the risk differs by ancestry; odds ratios describe groups, not a person’s fate; and the letters say nothing about familial APP or presenilin disease, which is a different mechanism.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Odds ratios describe groups, not fate

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “APOE ε4 (Arg112/Arg158) = strongest late-onset AD risk allele: OR ~3 one copy, ~15 two copies — risk, not diagnosis”, “Familial APP/PSEN AD < 1% · CSF Aβ42/40 ↓ · APOE genotype guides ARIA risk on donanemab”.

cues.text: APOE epsilon 4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer disease but does not diagnose it, while rare APP or presenilin mutations cause familial early-onset disease, and the laboratory supports diagnosis with the CSF amyloid beta 42 to 40 ratio.

props.label: ε4 (Arg/Arg): OR ~3 one copy, ~15 two — risk, not diagnosis
APP/PSEN < 1% · CSF Aβ42/40 ↓ · APOE → ARIA risk

explanation.what: Plain language: one common gene variant (APOE ε4) raises the chance of late-onset Alzheimer disease without deciding it, while a few rare family mutations cause early-onset disease directly. Scientific terms: APOE ε2/ε3/ε4, residues 112 and 158, odds ratio, late-onset AD (LOAD), early-onset familial AD, APP, PSEN1, PSEN2, γ-secretase, amyloid-β 40/42, CSF Aβ42/40 ratio, ARIA.
explanation.why: ApoE isoforms differ at two residues that change how they bind lipids, receptors and Aβ. Familial mutations in APP or presenilins cause Aβ overproduction. As Aβ42 deposits in the brain, CSF Aβ42 falls; dividing by Aβ40 corrects for each person’s overall Aβ production.
explanation.measure: APOE genotyping (ε2/ε3/ε4 from codons 112 and 158). Odds vs ε3/ε3: ε3/ε4 3.2, ε4/ε4 14.9, ε2/ε3 0.6 (Liu 2013). CSF Aβ42 ↓, Aβ40 ≈, Aβ42/40 ↓ in AD; pre-analytics critical (Hansson 2019). Donanemab AUR requires APOE genotyping for ARIA risk (Jeon 2025).
explanation.differs: APOE ε4 (common risk allele, raises odds) vs APP/PSEN1/PSEN2 mutations (rare, cause familial early-onset AD); CSF Aβ42 alone vs Aβ42/40 ratio (normalized).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: counsel an ε4 result as risk rather than diagnosis, identify APP/PSEN as rare familial causes, know CSF Aβ42 falls in AD, and recognize lecanemab/donanemab as approved anti-amyloid antibodies.

right.label: APP / PSEN1 / PSEN2
points: Cause familial early-onset AD via Aβ overproduction

mnemonic.text: ApoE4 has two Rs (Arg112, Arg158) — Risk, Risk. ApoE2 has two Cs — Cushioned. ApoE3 is the common middle, C then R.
mnemonic.explanation: Links the two distinguishing residues to the risk direction of each allele.
mnemonic.limitation: Risk size varies by ancestry; odds ratios describe groups, not individuals; familial APP/PSEN disease is a separate mechanism.

analogyLimitations: Odds ratios are from one meta-analysis and vary by ancestry.
takeaway: APOE epsilon 4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer disease but does not diagnose it, while rare APP or presenilin mutations cause familial early-onset disease, and the laboratory supports diagnosis with the CSF amyloid beta 42 to 40 ratio.

questions.stem: An APOE genotyping assay detects arginine at both residue 112 and residue 158 on both alleles. What is the genotype?

options.rationale: Correct. ApoE4 is Arg112/Arg158; two such alleles make ε4/ε4.
Incorrect. An ε2 allele would carry cysteine at both residues.

questions.stem: A cognitively normal 60-year-old is ε3/ε4. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: The odds of Alzheimer disease are raised about three-fold versus ε3/ε3, but the result does not diagnose or guarantee disease
options.rationale: Correct. Liu 2013 meta-analysis: ε3/ε4 OR 3.2 vs ε3/ε3; ε4 is a risk factor.

options.text: Alzheimer disease is certain within ten years
options.rationale: Incorrect. An odds ratio describes increased risk, not certainty.

options.text: This is familial early-onset Alzheimer disease
options.rationale: Incorrect. Familial early-onset AD is mainly due to APP, PSEN1 or PSEN2 mutations.
Incorrect. ε2 is the protective allele (ε2/ε3 OR 0.6).

questions.stem: Which CSF pattern is typical of Alzheimer disease?

options.text: Decreased Aβ42 with little change in Aβ40, so a decreased Aβ42/40 ratio
options.rationale: Correct. Hansson 2019: Aβ42 falls, Aβ40 does not differ significantly, and the ratio falls.

options.text: Increased Aβ42 and increased Aβ42/40 ratio
options.rationale: Incorrect. Aβ42 deposits in the brain and CSF levels fall.
Incorrect. Aβ40 did not differ significantly between groups.

options.text: An APOE ε4 genotype in CSF
options.rationale: Incorrect. APOE is a genotype from DNA, not a CSF amyloid measurement.

references.citation: Liu CC, Kanekiyo T, Xu H, Bu G. Apolipoprotein E and Alzheimer disease: risk, mechanisms and therapy. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(2):106-118.
references.usedFor: Allele frequencies 8.4/77.9/13.7%; ~40% ε4 in AD; ApoE 299 aa, ~34 kDa; isoforms differ at 112/158 (Cys/Arg); lipid transport and Aβ binding; Aβ 40 or 42 aa from APP; early-onset familial AD < 1% due to APP/PSEN1/PSEN2 (γ-secretase components) via Aβ overproduction; ε4 strongest LOAD risk factor; ORs vs ε3/ε3 (2.6, 3.2, 14.9; ε2 0.6) and ancestry variation; ε4 carriers lower CSF Aβ42.

references.citation: Hansson O, Lehmann S, Otto M, Zetterberg H, Lewczuk P. Advantages and disadvantages of the use of the CSF Amyloid β (Aβ) 42/40 ratio in the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease. Alzheimers Res Ther. 2019;11(1):34.
references.usedFor: CSF Aβ42 decreased in AD dementia, Aβ40 not significantly different; ratio normalizes for total Aβ (Aβ40 most abundant) and improves classification and PET concordance; tubes, handling and storage are critical pre-analytical factors.

references.citation: Jeon SY, Byun MS, Choi HJ, et al. Eligibility for lecanemab and donanemab in Korea under Appropriate Use Recommendations. Alzheimers Dement. 2025;21(11):e70875.
references.usedFor: Lecanemab FDA approval July 2023, donanemab 2024; donanemab AUR requires APOE genotyping for ARIA risk management.

references.citation: Belachew EA, Peterson GM, Bezabhe WM. Comparative effects of angiotensin II stimulating and inhibiting antihypertensives on dementia risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Geroscience. 2025;47(4):5525-5541.
references.usedFor: Evidence for the accuracy flag only: observational studies favoured Ang-II stimulating over Ang-II inhibiting drugs (which include ACE inhibitors) for dementia risk; the RCT meta-analysis was non-significant.

claims.text: APOE allele frequencies; isoforms differ at residues 112 and 158.
ε4 strongest LOAD risk factor; ORs vs ε3/ε3; ε2 protective; ancestry variation.
Familial early-onset AD < 1% of AD; APP/PSEN1/PSEN2; Aβ overproduction; γ-secretase.
CSF Aβ42 ↓, Aβ40 unchanged, Aβ42/40 ratio ↓ and better classification; pre-analytics critical.
Lecanemab (July 2023) and donanemab (2024) FDA-approved; APOE genotyping for ARIA risk under donanemab AUR.
Penetrance by age (~30% by 75, >50% by 85); Aβ42 neurotoxic vs Aβ40 neuroprotective; PSEN raises Aβ42:Aβ40; ACE converts Aβ42 → Aβ40; aducanumab discontinuation; cholinergic/NMDA drug list.
claims.note: Not taught as facts; no open source read for these, and the ACE claim conflicts with trial evidence (see flag).

accuracyFlags.issue: The reviewer states that ACE inhibition “is a risk factor for cognitive impairment/AD onset” (Hit 7, Trap 2). A 2025 meta-analysis (Belachew) found lower dementia risk with Ang-II stimulating antihypertensives than with Ang-II inhibiting ones (including ACE inhibitors) in observational studies only; the RCT meta-analysis was non-significant. A causal risk is not established.
